content.text: The cause is in `solution/core.py`: when a new interval is contained in the previous one, the code sets the end to the new interval's end (`b`) instead of the max of the two ends, so `(1, 4)` followed by `(2, 3)` shrinks to `(1, 3)`. I'll rewrite the merge loop to use `max` and keep the touching and duplicate rules.

content.text: The visible suite now passes (2 passed). I changed only `solution/core.py`. The cause was in the merge loop: when a new interval was contained in the previous one, the code set the merged end to the new interval's end instead of the larger of the two, so `(1, 4)` followed by `(2, 3)` shrank to `(1, 3)`. The fix sets the end to `max(pb, b)`, and I restructured the loop so that exact duplicates are skipped first, then overlaps and containment are merged, and touching intervals are joined only when `join_touching=True`. Spot checks match the intended semantics: `[(1,4),(2,3)]` gives `[(1,4)]`, `[(1,2),(2,3)]` gives `[(1,2),(2,3)]` without the flag and `[(1,3)]` with it, and duplicate points collapse. The public `merge` signature and the `ValueError` on reversed intervals are unchanged, and nothing under `tests/` was touched.
